Maya (AcmeChat): Hey team — starting ~08:04 UTC we're getting a flood of 429s from your API in prod, chatflow failing for ~20% of user requests. No code changes on our side. Any idea?

Sarah (Support): Sorry to hear that, @Maya. Can you paste a few sample request IDs or a sample curl? Also which region and model are you hitting? :eyes:

Maya (AcmeChat): Sample curl (anonymized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***\" 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","input":"hi","conversation_id":"abc-123"}'
```
We see 429s intermittently with response body: `{\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\"}` and headers like `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0` sometimes. Region: eu-west-1.

Joel (Oncall): Thanks, @Maya — can you share tenant/org id and approximate RPS? Also did you spike around minute boundaries (cron/batch) or steady increase?

Maya (AcmeChat): Tenant: acme-chat-prod, avg steady 18 req/s per node, short bursts up to 80 req/s for a few seconds when a push arrives. No cron.

Priya (Infra): Noted. Quick checks: 1) Are you using streaming or non-streaming? 2) Do you have client-side retries with no jitter? Retries can amplify minute-windowed limits.

Maya (AcmeChat): Non-streaming for these flows. We have exponential backoff but our max concurrency per process is high (50). No jitter.

Sarah (Support): That might explain amplification. Two suggestions while we triage: 1) Add jitter to retry backoff, 2) drop client concurrency to 8-10 per worker as a safety cap, 3) enable server-side request inspection for a 5m window so infra can see the exact headers.

Joel (Oncall): I'm pulling logs for tenant acme-chat-prod in eu-west-1 now. @deploy-bot any deploys around 08:00-08:10 UTC?

deploy-bot: deploys/acme-chat-prod to eu-west-1 by pipeline #42 completed at 07:58:12 UTC — image tag `chat-v1.27.3`.

Priya (Infra): I see many short spikes in our edge proxies for that tenant — bursts line up with 08:04:05 and 08:05:13 — token bucket drained and reset windows hit. We have a per-tenant RPM/TPM enforced at the edge plus a per-route concurrent inflight cap.

Maya (AcmeChat): Hmm those timestamps match our push notifications. Users hit a notification which fans out to many open websockets then triggers /generate calls.

Sarah (Support): Can you throttle fanout client-side? Or add random jitter 0-300ms when handling incoming push to smooth spikes.

Maya (AcmeChat): We'll try reducing concurrency and add jitter. Do you recommend any server-side config changes?

Priya (Infra): Short-term we can raise the tenant burst window for acme-chat-prod by 2x for 1 hour while you roll out client changes — but need formal approval from account team if sustained. Also we can enable per-request prefix caching for identical conversation_id tokens to cut load if many identical requests happen.

Joel (Oncall): Action items: 1) @Maya reduce concurrency and add jitter (customer). 2) @Priya temporarily raise burst allowance (infra) — I'll monitor. 3) @Sarah follow up with account for approval if they want longer bump.

Maya (AcmeChat): Doing client changes now, ETA 25m. We'll report if 429s stop. Thanks. :pray:

Sarah (Support): Ping me when done and we'll monitor the 1h window. Also share a handful of failing request-ids if any recur.

Priya (Infra): From infra side: logs show `x-rate-limit-reset` aligned to minute boundaries; if you see recurring minute-boundary 429s, consider smoothing logic to avoid hitting the exact reset edge.

Maya (AcmeChat): Update: implemented jitter + cap to 10 concurrency, deploying in 12m.

Joel (Oncall): Monitoring: error rate for acme-chat-prod in eu-west-1 already down 60% since 08:22 UTC. Keep an eye for retries causing later small spikes.

Maya (AcmeChat): Confirmed — after deploy, 429s dropped to <1%. Thanks everyone.

Sarah (Support): Great — leaving this thread open for 24h. If you want the temporary burst bump extended, we'll route to account. :thumbsup:

Priya (Infra): Filed a short runbook note: "customer push-fanout -> minute-bucket drain -> 429s" and recommended client jitter + concurrency cap.

Maya (AcmeChat): Thanks all, closing on our side but will reach out if anything else crops up.
